references.text: This is the direct prophecy that John 12:38 quoted, where the question of who has believed in the Lord's revealed arm is raised.
Paul quoted the same verse from Isaiah to emphasize that not all Israelites have listened to the gospel, paralleling John's usage.
The context for the quote in John 12:38, where Isaiah describes the Lord's arm as revealed to all nations, leads directly into the question of faith in chapter 53.
The description of the suffering servant who has 'no beauty or majesty' explains why few believed the message, which is the theme of the quote in John 12:38.
